clue.text: Small thing Fellow sliced off in stew, finished in coastal location

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit'

indicators.note: being in a stew is being in a muddle, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
something finished is over

explanation.surface: Someone trims a bit of a fellow's portion into the stew and finishes up at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in stew' scrambles F plus SLICEDOFF into ECLIFFSOFD. The four lights read as one phrase: the famous chalk cliffs on the Kent coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The chalk cliffs above the Kentish port are a landmark of the English shoreline, a place on the coast.

clue.text: Extend war, invade D-day, enter Normandy firstly

indicators.note: firstly asks for the opening letter of each of the five preceding words

explanation.surface: A general broadens the conflict by landing on D-Day in Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen something is to broaden or enlarge it, a synonym of extend.

clue.text: Trickster's troubled evil reign

indicators.note: troubled suggests disturbed, so the letters of evil reign are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A con artist's rule is a wicked, unsettled one.
explanation.definitionFit: One who inveigles coaxes people by deceit, so the word is a synonym for a cheat or con man.

clue.text: Uninhibited courage top to bottom over year

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another means it sits above it
the first letter of the word is moved from the top down to the bottom in this down clue

parts.note: heart means courage, as in 'take heart'

explanation.surface: A free spirit's boldness turns everything upside down for a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top to bottom' shifts the first letter of the courage word to its end; 'over' then stacks that above the year letter, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is frank and coarse, lacking prudishness, so it fits unrestrained.

clue.text: See 1
US volume on its war role? Exactly

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another is placed above it

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of litre, a unit of volume
the US fought as an ally in the world wars

explanation.surface: Was America's role in the war truly as a partner? Precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to US: America's part in the war was that of an ally.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally means to the letter, word for word, so precisely or exactly.

clue.text: Extremely lively after official set up film with enthusiasm

indicators.note: after places the outer letters of lively at the end of the rest
set up in a down clue means written upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is a match official
a vid is a short informal word for a video

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An excited referee arranges a lively film with great gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses the official because this is a down clue; 'Extremely' takes only the outer letters of 'lively', which come 'after' everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervid means ardent and impassioned, so doing something fervidly is doing it keenly.

clue.text: Plan postwar authority

definitions.meaning: to ... a scheme is to devise or plan it
the Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, NATO's command set up after the Second World War

explanation.definitionFit: To give form to a scheme is to plan it, and the acronym names NATO's postwar military headquarters in Europe.

clue.text: Payments securing rare quality fruit

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the payments word encloses the letter for rare

parts.note: fees are payments for services
R is an abbreviation for rare, as on steak menus
tone means character or quality, as in the tone of a place

explanation.surface: Fees protect an unusual standard of produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' wraps the payments round the rare letter. Freestone peaches are contrasted with clingstones, whose flesh sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: A freestone is a peach or plum whose flesh comes away easily from the stone.

clue.text: Over time Army regularly use it?

definitions.text: Over time Army regularly use it?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece goes over the second
regularly picks every other letter of the word Army, starting with the first

parts.note: a mo is a short time, as in 'half a mo'

explanation.surface: Soldiers routinely go through supplies of ammunition as time goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes A and M from 'Army', placed 'Over' MO. The whole clue also hints at the answer: bullets are what an army keeps using.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition, shortened, is the shells and cartridges that troops fire.

clue.text: See 1
Parade test by soldiers trainee can't finish

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British cars
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: the trainee word cannot reach its end, so it loses its last letter

parts.note: a cadet is a trainee in the forces or police

explanation.surface: A trainee fails to complete a parade drill with the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't finish' drops the final T of CADET. The MOT is Britain's yearly vehicle safety test.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcade is a procession of cars, a kind of parade.

clue.text: Blitz hero, ensign, busily no end helping others

indicators.note: a blitz is a violent attack, so the letters are blasted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: with no end, the word busily loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In the wartime bombing a hero and a young officer busily dash about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' cuts the Y from 'busily', leaving BUSIL; 'Blitz' then rearranges HERO, ENSIGN and BUSIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a good neighbour means friendly helpfulness towards those living around you, so it describes aiding others.

clue.text: Quisling's capital's big. Look!

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a big clothing size
lo is an old exclamation meaning look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: A traitor marvels at how large his city is.
explanation.walkthrough: Vidkun Quisling was the Norwegian collaborator of the Second World War, so his capital is Norway's.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway's capital was Quisling's seat of power when he led the puppet government.

clue.text: Removal of leader, say, in public, first of high rank

parts.note: overt means open or public

indicators.note: first of picks just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers or seats

explanation.surface: A coup is described openly, with a senior figure taking the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the definition as one example: an overthrow need not be of a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup that topples a ruler is an overthrow, ousting someone from power.

clue.text: Party held by the Italian great

indicators.note: held by means the party word sits inside the Italian article

parts.note: il is the Italian for the
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A party is thrown by an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A great, as a noun, is a celebrated figure, someone worshipped or admired by fans.

clue.text: Surveying plane until Dame's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread about anew

parts.note: taken as written
the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Wait until the Dame's programme goes out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges UNTIL and DAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveyors measure heights from a fixed reference level, the baseline used as zero.

clue.text: Short toilet break? Stop at sea!

indicators.note: break means smash up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
short asks for the word to be cut by its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A quick bathroom stop, and the sailors are told to halt!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims the final T, leaving TOILE, which 'break' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie to is the nautical term for bringing a ship nearly to a standstill, heading into the wind.

clue.text: Dish prepared in hacienda with little left?

indicators.note: prepared, as food is prepared, suggests the letters are worked into new form

parts.note: taken as written
L is the short form of left

explanation.surface: A meal made in a ranch house when there is not much food remaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges HACIENDA with L.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican tortilla rolled round a filling and baked in sauce, a food served at table.

clue.text: Roman object I'd given to Unionist with hesitation? It's left behind

parts.note: res is Latin for thing or object
taken as written, without the apostrophe
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A Roman relic I'd hand to a hesitant Unionist turns out to be leftover.
explanation.definitionFit: A residuum is the residue, what remains after the rest is removed.

clue.text: Nobleman's no power-that is weird!

indicators.note: no means without, so the power letter is removed

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman; the possessive adds no letter
P is the symbol for power in physics
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A lord without influence: how strange that is!
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes P from PEER, leaving EER, followed by IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, uncanny in a spooky way.

clue.text: Possibly presents two Yanks, outsiders

indicators.note: outsiders asks for the outer letters, first and last, of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Perhaps gifts arrive for two American strangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outsiders' takes T and O from 'two', then Y and S from 'Yanks'. 'Possibly' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Playthings are typical gifts for children, so presents may well be these.

clue.text: Area where top pilot suppresses resistance

indicators.note: suppresses means holds down, so the pilot word encloses the resistance letter

parts.note: an ace is a fighter pilot with many kills
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A region where a leading airman crushes the resistance movement.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land measure, 4,840 square yards.

clue.text: Fabric in a cap lancer raised

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cavalryman lifts his cap made of woollen cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'raised' reads ACAPLA from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft wool of a South American llama-like animal gives its name to the cloth woven from it.

clue.text: Work shows how at first Adolf Hitler battled with millions

indicators.note: battled suggests a struggle, so the letters fight their way into new order
at first asks for the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A book shows how the dictator first waged war against huge numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives A from 'Adolf'; 'battled' rearranges A with HITLER and MILLIONS into Tolkien's book title.
explanation.definitionFit: The posthumous Tolkien book of Middle-earth myths is a literary work.

clue.text: Heard extra large is better

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the letters are what the abbreviation sounds like when spoken

parts.note: XL is the clothing size for extra large

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that a bigger size is preferable.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the letters X and L make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to better is to surpass, which is what one does on outshining others.

clue.text: Tune's rising over good Baltic city

indicators.note: over means covering, so the reversed tune wraps round the good letter
rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: an air is a tune; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A melody climbs above a fine town on the Baltic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns AIR into RIA, which goes 'over' G, wrapping round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Latvia lies on the Gulf of Riga, an arm of the Baltic Sea.

clue.text: Second name showing discrimination?

definitions.meaning: the middle of a Roman's three names, the family or clan name
read as two words, a sign saying males are barred

explanation.definitionFit: A Roman's clan name came second, after the given name; split in two, the word reads as a ban on males.

clue.text: Making good, English company reaches high point in competitive field

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the word for an arena

parts.note: a ring is an arena for boxing or other contests
up means at a high point or on top

explanation.surface: An English firm recovers by reaching the summit in a crowded market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the English, company and high-point pieces inside the arena word; 'reaches' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Recouping a loss is recovering it, setting the account straight again.

clue.text: Warning as marines do?

parts.note: a la, from the French, means in the manner of, so 'as ... do'
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A signal raised the way soldiers at sea would raise it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'as marines do' is a la RM, in the style of the Royal Marines.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a signal that warns of danger.

clue.text: After war's start, get El Alamein in struggle — it's not the end

indicators.note: after says the rest follows the first letter of war
start asks for the opening letter of the word before it
in struggle means in turmoil, so these letters are tossed about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Once the war begins, head for the desert battle in North Africa, which is no conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' gives W; 'in struggle' rearranges GET EL ALAMEIN. The answer is the title of the Vera Lynn wartime song promising future reunion.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's title promises that parting is temporary, so a farewell is not final.

clue.text: See 29
